answer: An agent economy can tie each identity's influence to reputation imported from independent economies: a newcomer starts weak, and its standing in this meadow of agents grows only as verified records arrive from other networks, like a cedar whose roots reach beyond a single grove. Misbehaviour proven anywhere slashes standing everywhere at once, so one exposed fake burns the whole portfolio. To field a thousand Sybils, an attacker must build a thousand genuine histories across many separate economies, paying real work in each, instead of minting free identities in one place.
